Covered · Session 01M00 / M01

Orientation, readiness & business-question framing

Ask a question worth answering

Turn a broad concern into an evidence question, define what each row represents, and make the next decision explicit.

Try this session’s experiment →Study mode: notes and interactive lesson →Lab checkpoints →
Study toolkitLaboratoryMind mapInfographicsListenFull slides

What you can explain

  • Name the stakeholder, decision, population, and time horizon.
  • Distinguish the business problem from the software task.
  • Check grain, units, provenance, and tool readiness.

Start with the decision

Concern → stakeholder → action → evidence

A business problem describes a condition. A decision names a choice. An analytic question identifies evidence that could inform that choice.

Connect it to a business example

For a fictional museum café, ask whether next month's weekend staffing should change, then identify which service measure could inform that choice.

Define the evidence

Population → grain → variable → provenance

Grain states what one row represents. A customer may have several transactions; transaction counts are not customer counts.

Connect it to a business example

A row for each café visit supports a visit-level wait measure. Line-item rows must be reconciled before counting visits.

Set a measure and a guardrail

Numerator / eligible denominator → unit → target

A KPI needs an operational definition, reporting period, eligible population, and denominator. A guardrail limits harm or unacceptable data quality.

Connect it to a business example

Pair a service target with a missing-wait guardrail so a good rate cannot hide poor records.

Make reasoning inspectable

Observation → inference → assumption → next action

Software calculates. People judge whether evidence supports a recommendation. Keep observed facts separate from claims about causes or the future.

Connect it to a business example

Report what the available visits show, explain uncertainty, and propose a bounded check before a permanent decision.
